title: Digital Takes The Court For March Madness

facts.fact: The article reports that highlights of NCAA March Madness games that had not yet been played were created by thousands of Xbox gamers taking part in a Pontiac promotion.
facts.quote: have been played virtually by thousands of Xbox gamers taking part in a Pontiac promotion

facts.fact: Cingular Wireless was going to provide a digital "halftime show" for online viewers of the March Madness games.
facts.quote: Cingular Wireless will be providing a digital “halftime show” for online viewers

facts.fact: State Farm was going to help generate excuses for fans who wanted privacy to watch the games in the office.
facts.quote: State Farm will help generate excuses for fans trying to get some privacy to watch in the office.

facts.fact: The Adweek article "Digital Takes The Court For March Madness" was published on March 12, 2007.
Adweek's headline for a Rao's brand story describes a 4-minute film about family time in place of saucy product shots.
facts.quote: Rao’s Trades Saucy Product Shots for a 4-Minute Film About Family Time

facts.fact: Adweek reports that prediction market apps Polymarket, Kalshi and Novig face legal fights and NFL restrictions that limit where their ads can run.
facts.quote: Polymarket, Kalshi and Novig face legal fights and NFL restrictions that limit where their ads can run
